result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend showing no indicator at first, keeping previous results visible, and never using both loaders, and both give similar delay and minimum-display timings. B is more decisive: it picks one indicator, the trailing spinner, and explains why a skeleton causes layout jump when the result count varies. It also covers the no-results state and reduced motion. A splits the choice by state, which is reasonable but less clear, though it does add a useful point about stale responses. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the same core advice: don't add both loaders, hold off showing any indicator for about 250-300 ms, keep previous results visible, and keep the indicator up for a minimum time so it doesn't flicker. A commits to a single spinner, explains why a skeleton causes layout jump, and covers no-results announcements and reduced motion. B splits skeleton and spinner by state and adds handling of stale responses and throttled-network testing. Neither covers keyboard use of the list or error states, so their strengths balance out.
